title: Samut Sakhon to Bangkok: 2-Day Mahachai & City Trip | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 2-day, 1-night cross-province plan from Samut Sakhon to Bangkok. Ride the Mae Klong railway from Wongwian Yai to Mahachai, hit the seafood markets, then explore Thonburi, Wat Arun, ICONSIAM and Talat Phlu — with real times, prices and routes.

h1:
Samut Sakhon to Bangkok
2 Days: Mahachai Plus the City
intro: Mahachai and Bangkok sit closer together than most people think, and they're linked by something special: the Mae Klong railway, the Wongwian Yai–Mahachai line. One line takes you across the provincial border in about an hour, and the fare is just a few baht. So this plan spends day one in Mahachai and Samut Sakhon — the seafood markets, fresh catch straight off the boats, dried-shrimp and salted-fish souvenirs — then rides the train back into the city for a night in Thonburi. Day two is a walking tour of Wongwian Yai, Wat Arun, ICONSIAM and Talat Phlu. You can do the whole thing without a car. Here are the real times, prices and routes.
chips: 🚆 Mae Klong railway links two provinces

blocks.html: Samut Sakhon practically borders Bangkok. The town of Mahachai is about 20 miles by road from Thonburi, roughly a 40–60 minute drive depending on traffic on Rama II Road. But what makes this route especially fun is the Mae Klong railway on the Wongwian Yai–Mahachai stretch, which has connected the two towns since the reign of King Rama V. It's a relaxed ride, the fare is cheap, and the final station is a short walk from Mahachai market.

The theme of this trip is sea and city. Day one is all Mahachai — the wet market, the Thai Talay seafood market, the seafood itself, the souvenirs — then the train carries you back into Bangkok for a night around Wongwian Yai or Thonburi. Day two is Thonburi on foot and by boat, finishing with Wat Arun and ICONSIAM on the Chao Phraya. It works well for Bangkok locals who want a close weekend trip, and for out-of-towners who fly into Bangkok and want to add a seaside town to the mix.

blocks.text: The Mae Klong railway: the line that makes this trip possible

blocks.html: The Wongwian Yai–Mahachai train is the first leg of the Mae Klong railway. It leaves from Wongwian Yai station in Thonburi, runs through Talat Phlu, and ends at Mahachai station in Samut Sakhon, taking about an hour. The fare for the whole line is just 10 THB, and trains run frequently from morning until night, so you have plenty of flexibility — head out to Mahachai early and come back in the afternoon, or stay until evening.

items: From Wongwian Yai — the first morning train runs from around 05:30, with frequent departures through the day until the last evening train around 20:10, so you have several slots to choose from
Fare — Wongwian Yai to Mahachai is about 10 THB; short hops like Wongwian Yai–Talat Phlu are only a few baht. Buy your ticket at the station window or on board
Travel time — around an hour for the full line, a comfortable ride watching the trackside neighbourhoods roll by
Heading back to Bangkok — trains return from Mahachai to Wongwian Yai throughout the day too; always check the latest times at the station first, since the schedule can change

blocks.title: What to know about the train
blocks.html: Train times are adjusted from time to time, so before you go, check the latest schedule on the State Railway of Thailand website, or snap a photo of the timetable posted at the station. If you'd rather not gamble on departures, driving yourself or taking a van from Sai Tai Mai / Mo Chit into Mahachai is a more flexible option.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Seafood markets, the freshest catch, and fishing-town souvenirs

items.activity: Board the Mae Klong train at Wongwian Yai station
items.note: Take the early train and you'll reach Mahachai while the market is still busy. The fare is 10 THB and the ride takes about an hour, with relaxing views of the trackside communities. If you're driving, get onto Rama II Road before 8am to beat the traffic.

items.activity: Wander Mahachai wet market by the municipal pier
items.note: Open from morning until early afternoon — shrimp, shellfish, crab and fish straight off the boats, with retail prices lower than in the city. Come early while everything is still fresh and fully stocked. From Mahachai station it's a short walk to the market.

items.activity: Take the ferry across the Tha Chin River to Tha Chalom
items.note: Tha Chalom is an old community and Thailand's first sanitary district. The cross-river ferry costs only a few baht; wander among the old shophouses and the riverside fishing life — it's a great spot for photos.
This area has plenty of seafood restaurants. Try the big green mussels, steamed blue crab and fresh Mae Klong mackerel. Prices go by weight — pick your catch and have the kitchen cook it for you.

items.activity: Thai Talay market, the province's big seafood wholesale hub
items.note: Both fresh and dried goods at wholesale prices — dried shrimp, dried squid, salted fish and shrimp paste make great-value buys to take home. It's a little outside town, so hop on a songthaew or motorcycle taxi to get there.

items.activity: Pay your respects at Wat Chetsadaram, then try the local lod chong
items.note: Wat Chetsadaram is a royal temple in the centre of Mahachai. Nearby is the town's signature lod chong — soft, chewy noodles in rich coconut milk, a cooling treat before you head back.

items.activity: Buy processed-seafood souvenirs, then take the train back to Wongwian Yai
items.note: Salted fish, dried shrimp, shrimp paste, fish sauce and snakeskin gourami fish — lots of shops to choose from, so compare prices before you buy. Then catch an afternoon or evening train back into Bangkok, arriving at Wongwian Yai in time to check into your hotel.

blocks.title: Tips for buying seafood
blocks.html: Buy fresh items last, right before you leave, and bring a cooler or insulated bag. For dried goods like dried shrimp and squid, smell and check the colour before buying — the good stuff has no musty smell and isn't an unnaturally bright red. If you're carrying it onto the train, well-sealed dried goods are easier to manage.

Mahachai is one of Thailand's major fishing and seafood-processing towns, so the souvenirs revolve around the sea. Here are the things people most often buy to take home, ranked by popularity and value. Dried goods are the easiest to carry back on the train.

items.name: Dried shrimp
items.blurb: The star souvenir of Mahachai. Look for a natural orange-pink colour, firm flesh and a flavour that isn't too salty — great for making nam prik, in salads, or as a snack. Thai Talay market stocks several grades.

items.name: Salted fish & salted mackerel
items.blurb: Many kinds of salted fish from the local fishing boats. Fried, they go perfectly with rice porridge, they keep well, and they make an easy souvenir for anyone who likes simple, no-fuss food.

items.name: Shrimp paste (kapi)
items.blurb: Shrimp paste made from Gulf of Thailand krill — fragrant, with a greyish-purple colour, used in nam prik kapi and curries. A well-known local product that fans of Thai food often pick up.

items.name: Dried squid
items.blurb: Big dried squid with a sweet flesh, grilled or fried as a snack. Look for a natural light-brown colour rather than an unnaturally pale white.

items.name: Sun-dried snakeskin gourami
items.blurb: The snakeskin gourami around here has firm flesh and just the right amount of fat — fry it crisp and eat it with hot steamed rice. Sold by the piece or by the kilo, and easy to carry home.

items.name: Pure fish sauce
items.blurb: Fish sauce from locally fermented anchovies — a clear brown colour, fragrant, useful in any kitchen. A souvenir that actually gets used rather than left in the cupboard.

items.name: Fish snacks & shredded squid
items.blurb: Processed snacks that kids and adults both love. The souvenir shops around Mahachai let you sample before you buy, making this an easy, crowd-pleasing gift.

blocks.text: Which side to spend the night

blocks.html: This plan suggests spending the night on the Bangkok side, around Wongwian Yai–Thonburi, because that's where the train from Mahachai pulls in, and the next morning you can start exploring Thonburi right away. The area has hotels and stays along the Chao Phraya at every level, from budget hostels to riverside-view hotels. If you'd rather give Mahachai a full day before heading back, you can also overnight in Samut Sakhon town first and come into Bangkok the next morning — you'll just shuffle the order of the day-two stops a little.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Wongwian Yai, Talat Phlu, Wat Arun, and ICONSIAM on the Chao Phraya

items.activity: Start the morning in Talat Phlu, Thonburi's old food quarter
items.note: Talat Phlu is a famous food neighbourhood — fried Chinese chives, pork satay, duck noodles, Thai sweets. It's an easy place to graze for breakfast. Take the BTS Silom Line and get off at Talat Phlu station.

items.activity: Visit Wat Arun Ratchawararam (the Temple of Dawn)
items.note: The riverside prang stands about 82 metres tall, open for visits roughly 08:00–18:00. Cross by boat from Tha Tian or walk over from the Thonburi side. The morning light is gentle and good for photos.

items.activity: Riverside lunch around Tha Din Daeng–Khlong San
items.note: The Thonburi bank of the Chao Phraya has plenty of riverside restaurants and cafes. Pick a spot to relax and catch the breeze before the afternoon.

items.activity: Stroll ICONSIAM on the Chao Phraya River
items.note: This riverside mall on the Khlong San side has SookSiam, an indoor floating-market replica with Thai food from across the country, plus photo spots along the Chao Phraya. Easy to spend the whole afternoon here in the cooler hours.

items.activity: Watch the sunset over the Chao Phraya to close the trip
items.note: The River Park in front of ICONSIAM or a rooftop riverside bar both look out over the river and the Phra Nakhon side — a lovely place to end the trip before you part ways.

blocks.title: Tips for exploring Thonburi
blocks.html: Thonburi is best explored by boat and BTS. The Chao Phraya express boats and cross-river ferries link the various piers for just a few baht, while the BTS Silom Line has stations at Wongwian Yai, Talat Phlu and Krung Thonburi near ICONSIAM. Planning your stops along the boat and skytrain routes saves more time and money than hiring a car.

blocks.text: Extra stops if you have time

items.name: Phan Thai Norasing Shrine
items.blurb: A spiritual stop beside Khlong Khok Kham in Samut Sakhon, where people pray over honesty and their careers. There's a life-size statue of Phan Thai Norasing — worth a detour if you're driving.

items.name: Samut Sakhon salt fields
items.blurb: Salt fields along Rama II Road. In the dry season you'll see rows of white salt mounds — pretty for evening photos, and a glimpse of one of the province's traditional livelihoods.

items.name: Wat Paknam, Phasi Charoen
items.blurb: A glass pagoda and a giant Buddha image on the Thonburi side, a popular temple stop not far from the Talat Phlu area. An easy add-on after the day-two plan.

items: 1 night's stay — around the Wongwian Yai–Thonburi area, roughly ฿600–1,800/night (hostels are cheaper, riverside-view hotels cost more)
Train / boat / BTS — the Wongwian Yai–Mahachai train is about 20 THB round trip, cross-river ferries and boats a few baht each, BTS priced by distance; a few hundred baht total for the whole trip
Entry fees — Wat Arun charges around a hundred baht; the other temples and ICONSIAM are free
Food — a Mahachai seafood meal runs about ฿150–400; city meals vary by where you choose
Souvenirs — budget ฿300–800 and you'll come home with a full bag of dried seafood
Whole trip — roughly ฿1,500–3,500/person, not counting travel to Bangkok

faq.q: Can I combine Samut Sakhon and Bangkok into one trip?
faq.a: Easily. Mahachai is about 20 miles by road from Thonburi, and the Mae Klong railway on the Wongwian Yai–Mahachai stretch runs directly between them, taking about an hour for a 10 THB fare. A 2-day, 1-night plan fits perfectly: day one in Mahachai, a night in Thonburi, and Bangkok on day two.

faq.q: Where do I catch the Wongwian Yai–Mahachai Mae Klong train, and how much is it?
faq.a: Board at Wongwian Yai station in Thonburi. The fare for the full line to Mahachai is about 10 THB, with trains running from around 05:30 in the morning until about 20:10 at night, and a journey time of roughly one hour. Before you go, check the latest schedule on the railway website or the board at the station.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Mahachai market?
faq.a: The Mahachai wet market by the municipal pier is busiest in the morning, so aim to go before noon while the seafood is still fresh and fully stocked — by the afternoon many items start to run out. The early train from Wongwian Yai gets you there at the right time.

faq.q: Can I do this route without a car?
faq.a: Especially well, in fact, because this trip is designed around taking the Mae Klong railway across the provincial border. On the Bangkok side you get around by the BTS Silom Line and Chao Phraya boats, and in Mahachai the station is a short walk from the market. You can see it all without driving.

faq.q: Should I stay on the Mahachai side or the Bangkok side?
faq.a: This plan recommends staying on the Bangkok side, around Wongwian Yai–Thonburi, because the train from Mahachai pulls in here and you can start exploring Thonburi first thing the next morning. But if you want a full day in Mahachai, you can overnight in Samut Sakhon town first and come into Bangkok the following morning.
